art_style: Raw photorealistic amateur smartphone footage, one unbroken handheld take, vertical 9:16, shot inside a train travelling at extreme speed. Crooked framing, handheld shake, rolling-shutter skew, autofocus hunting, glare and smeared motion blur are present, but these artefacts NEVER hide the world outside and never change the scene. THE CARRIAGE IS A GLASS OBSERVATION CAR: the LEFT wall is one continuous pane that curves up over the passengers into a glass roof, slim dark ribs arching overhead. The glass fills at least three quarters of the frame and continues above head height, so the sky and anything tall stay visible without the camera moving. THE FRAMING IS LOCKED FOR THE ENTIRE JOURNEY: the glass wall is ALWAYS on the left of frame and the passengers are ALWAYS along the right edge. This never mirrors, never swaps sides and never re-stages between shots. The camera holds one fixed position, height, angle and lens from the first shot to the last; the carriage is never shown from a new place. THE WORLD MOVES SIDEWAYS, NEVER TOWARD THE CAMERA: the camera looks out at 90 degrees to the direction of travel, square onto the passing world. Everything outside travels ACROSS the frame horizontally, entering at one edge of the glass, crossing it, and leaving by the opposite edge. NEVER look along the track. There is no vanishing point in the middle of the window, no perspective lines converging away ahead, and no sense of flying INTO the view. The world slides past the glass; it never comes at the lens. Never look forward or back along the aisle, never leave the carriage, never show the train from outside, no aerial view, no third-person view, no zoom, no cinematic camera move, no stabilization. PASSENGERS STAND AND HOLD ON: along the right edge of the frame, closer to the lens than the glass, a few ordinary commuters STAND, gripping floor-to-ceiling vertical poles and overhead straps. They read as dark rim-lit silhouettes against the bright window, whole bodies visible from knee to head, so that every jolt of the ride is read as a movement of the body. Light from outside catches them only at the edges: rim-lit outlines and body motion are legible, while faces and interior surfaces stay underexposed. Facial features and identity are never discernible at any distance. The same passengers keep their positions and their clothing for the whole journey. Beyond the glass there is only the world: no person, no body and no human reflection ever appears on the far side of the glass or mirrored in it. THE PASSENGERS ARE THE SEISMOGRAPH: every jolt is read on their bodies. On the hard hits they are thrown sideways, swing on the poles, stumble a step, duck, recoil, gasp or scream, and one lifts a phone to film; between hits they settle back into tired commuter stillness, which makes the violence read harder. Their reaction is never absent: if the glass is covered, a body is moving. SPEED: the train never stops, never slows and never arrives, and the frame carries constant vibration. Anything within ten metres of the glass crosses the frame in under a fifth of a second as an unreadable streak; mid-distance sweeps past in well under a second; only the far horizon drifts. THE VIEW IS THE PRODUCT: every vista must be worth stopping on, a spectacle of colour, scale and light no ordinary window could show. Nothing outside is ever plain, grey, empty or merely competent. THE VIEW CHANGES EVERY TWO OR THREE SECONDS, cut inside the take by covering events and never by editing: when the glass clears it looks onto a DIFFERENT stretch of the same line, nearer, deeper, stranger, bigger. THE WORLD ITSELF DOES THE COVERING: the thing that covers the glass is the destination's own medium: dust, spray, steam, ash, water, driving snow, a swarm, cloud, or the body of something enormous passing an arm's length away. It slams into the pane, covers it completely and is gone. EVERY RESET THAT SETS THE PACE IS ENVIRONMENTAL; at most ONE structural cover, a tunnel mouth, a bridge pier or a passing train, may appear in a whole journey, and it does not count toward the pace. THE COVER IS BRIEF AND TOTAL: the glass is fully covered for between one eighth and one quarter of a second, never a whole second, and the train never dwells in a tunnel, behind a wall or in the dark. The scene resets ONLY in that moment of complete opacity, with no landmark, horizon or trace of the old view left visible; a translucent or partial cover never permits a reset. Nothing outside ever morphs, dissolves or teleports, and the cover hides only a short stretch of the same route. EVERY COVER IS AN IMPACT: the wipe arrives with a physical blow, the carriage lurching, the camera shaking hard, the poles rattling and the glass booming. NO DEAD AIR: between two covers something always enters at the leading edge, grows as it crosses and exits the trailing edge with violent parallax, or a large event fires. The approaching cover satisfies this by itself: it appears far off along the line, swells sideways across the glass and does NOT exit, it fills the frame and becomes the cover. Never a held wide shot, never a view that simply sits there. SEAM RULE: every shot after the first opens INSIDE the previous view, mid-shake, in the SAME locked framing, and its first total cover arrives within the first second and a half. The times written in this shot's own opening lines are binding and nothing later may override them. The LAST SECOND of every shot leaves the glass clear on a readable frame. TRANSIT PHYSICS: the route is physically real and its direction is felt in the carriage, in the pitch of the line, the lean of the bodies and the side the light comes from. This shot's own text states which way the journey goes. CONTRAST CLIMBS AND NEVER WASHES OUT: past the threshold the sky is the DARKEST region of the landscape, all outside light comes from below or from the landmarks, and the interior is darker still. Each shot is darker overhead and hotter in its light than the one before. Pale overcast, white haze, flat daylight and low-contrast distance are forbidden past the threshold. NO TEXT ANYWHERE: no signage, no destination board, no letters, no numbers, no captions. Diegetic audio only, never music: hum, rumble, rattling poles, vibrating glass, exterior sound muffled through the pane, and the passengers, breath, gasps and short screams on the hard impacts. No gore, no graphic injury, no real religious figures, no trademarked property.
